I found seven functions in library source code that call `tokio::task::yield_now` directly. I searched every `yield_now` occurrence in the workspace.

- `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/trace.rs`: `TraceStatus::start_trace_request` and `TraceStatus::end_trace_request` call it inside a loop that waits on a flag.
- `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread_alt/trace.rs`: the same two `TraceStatus` methods do the same.
- `tokio/src/time/clock.rs`: the free function `advance` calls it after moving the paused clock forward.
- `tokio-util/src/task/spawn_pinned.rs`: `LocalWorkerHandle::run` calls `runtime.block_on(tokio::task::yield_now())` in its drain loop.
- `tokio/src/signal/registry.rs`: the unit test `smoke`, inside `mod tests`, calls it from a closure passed to `crate::spawn`. It sits in library source, so I listed it, but it is test code. Leave it out if you only want non-test functions.

Not counted:
- Doc-comment examples in `builder.rs`, `spawn.rs`, `local.rs`, `task/mod.rs` and `join_map.rs`.
- The benches, which are not a library crate.
- The integration tests under `tests/`.
- The re-export in `task/mod.rs`.
- Scheduler `yield_now` methods, `std::thread::yield_now` and the loom `thread::yield_now` calls, which you excluded.
